entities.summary:
Louis de Gorrevod was a Roman Catholic bishop and cardinal who played a significant role in the Counter-Reformation movement. Born into a noble family in France, Louis rose through the ranks of the Catholic Church to become the Archbishop of Bordeaux and a key advisor to Pope Clement VII. His efforts to reform the Church's teachings and practices helped shape the theology of the time.

De Gorrevod's influence extended beyond his own diocese, as he worked closely with other prominent figures in the Counter-Reformation, including Charles de Guise and Cardinal Jean du Bellay. He was a strong advocate for the authority of Scripture and the importance of tradition in understanding Christian doctrine.

Despite facing opposition from Protestant reformers, Louis de Gorrevod remained committed to his faith and continued to serve the Catholic Church until his death in 1535. His legacy as a key figure in the Counter-Reformation has endured, with many historians recognizing his contributions to the development of Catholic theology during this critical period.

The 1540s saw the rise of powerful Protestant leaders such as Martin Luther and John Calvin, who challenged the authority of the Catholic Church. Louis de Gorrevod's efforts to counter these challenges helped ensure the survival of Catholicism in France.

Louis de Gorrevod's significance can be seen in his role as a mediator between the Catholic Church and the French monarchy, which played a crucial role in shaping the country's religious landscape during this period.
